`spigot_app()` adds `spigot.js` to every page it serves, after jQuery and Shiny's own
script. It defines `window.spigot`. It is plain JavaScript with no build step, and needs only
what every current browser has: `fetch`, `Promise`, `URL` and `AbortController`.

For a page that `spigot_app()` does not serve, such as a `shiny::fluidPage()` in a classic
Shiny app, attach `spigot_dependency()` to it.

## Calling the API

```js
spigot.get(path, query, options)
spigot.del(path, query, options)
spigot.post(path, body, options)
spigot.put(path, body, options)
spigot.request(method, path, options)
```

Each returns a promise of the reply.

**`path`** is relative to the API: `"items"` and `"/items"` both mean `api/items` (with the
default prefix), resolved against the page's URL. The app therefore keeps working under a
subpath. `spigot.base` holds the resolved API URL.

**`query`** is an object of query-string parameters. Arrays repeat the parameter
(`{id: [1, 2]}` gives `id=1&id=2`), and `null` or `undefined` values are left out.

**`body`** is sent as JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`, strings included. These
are sent unchanged, with the browser's own content type: `FormData`, `URLSearchParams`,
`Blob`, `ArrayBuffer` and typed arrays. To send plain text, wrap it in a `Blob`. A binary
body needs `#* @parser octet` on the endpoint.

**`options`** is an object with any of:

* `query`, `body`: as above, for `spigot.request()`.
* `headers`: extra request headers, as an object or a `Headers`.
* `timeout`: milliseconds. If no reply has arrived by then, the request is aborted and the
  promise rejects with a `SpigotError` whose `status` is `0`. The time counts from the call,
  including any wait for the session.

The reply is parsed by its content type: JSON gives the value, an empty body gives `null`,
and anything else gives the text.

## Errors: `spigot.SpigotError`

A call rejects with a `spigot.SpigotError` (a subclass of `Error`) when the reply is not 2xx
or when no reply arrives:

* `status`: the HTTP status, or `0` for a timeout or network failure.
* `message`: the JSON reply's `error` field if it has one, else the HTTP status text.
* `body`: the parsed reply.

```js
try {
  const rows = await spigot.get("forecast", { sku: "A1", h: 12 });
  draw(rows);
} catch (err) {
  if (!(err instanceof spigot.SpigotError)) throw err;
  if (err.status === 0) showOffline();
  else showError(err.message);
}
```

An endpoint chooses its error status by setting `res$status` and returning a list with an
`error` element. Some errors come from spigot or Shiny rather than your endpoints:

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `{"error": "session required", ...}` | No live session token, with `require_session = TRUE` |
| 403 | `{"error": "cross-origin request refused"}` | The request came from a page on another origin |
| 404, 405 | plumber's JSON | No such endpoint, or the wrong method for it |
| 413 | plain text | The body is over Shiny's size limit (`max_request_size`) |
| 500 | `{"error": ...}` | The endpoint threw an error |

## The session

Every request carries the tab's Shiny session token in an `X-Spigot-Session` header, which
is how `spigot_session(req)` finds the tab in R. Requests made before the session has
started wait for it.

* `spigot.ready`: a promise that resolves with the token once the session has started.
* `spigot.sessionId`: the token, or `null` before then. After Shiny reconnects, requests
  use the new session's token.

## Events from R

`spigot.on(event, fn)` calls `fn(data, event)` for each event that R sends with
`spigot_emit()` or `spigot_broadcast()`, and returns a function that removes the listener.
`spigot.off(event, fn)` removes `fn`; `spigot.off(event)` removes all of that event's
listeners. A listener that throws does not stop the others, and its error still reaches the
console.

```js
const stop = spigot.on("job:progress", (p) => {
  bar.value = p.done / p.total;
  if (p.done === p.total) stop();
});
```

Events that arrive before a listener is registered are dropped, and an event can arrive
before the HTTP reply to the request that caused it. See
`vignette("reactivity", package = "spigot")`.

## Links on nested pages

A page below the top level, such as `/docs/intro`, gets a `<base href>` that points at the
app root, so its relative URLs mean the same as on every other page. `spigot.js` keeps plain
clicks on `href="#section"` links on the page instead of following the base to the app
root. See `?spigot_page`.
